title: THE BLAME PIE
goal: Owning your part is different from taking all the blame.
steps: 1. Imagine A Pie — Imagine a pie that stands for everything that caused the situation. Blame Pie — breathe naturally.
2. Share The Slices — In your mind, give slices to your choices, other people, circumstances, systems, timing, and chance.
3. Check The Whole — Make sure all slices together equal 100. Blame Pie — split duty.
4. Find Your Slice — Focus only on your true share.
5. Choose Repair — Picture one repair for your slice. Let the rest stay outside your responsibility. Blame Pie — next action.

title: THE LIFE DIRECTION TEST
goal: A thought can sound true and still drive badly.
steps: 1. Picture — Picture two arrows. Life Direction — feel support.
2. Make Room — One shows the next hour if you obey the thought; the other reveals what unfolds over sixty minutes when you make room for it but follow a chosen value.
3. Name Likely — Name the likely behaviour at each arrow’s end. Life Direction — split duty.
4. Select Direction — Select by direction, not by mental volume. Life Direction — next action.

title: CLOSE ONE DOOR FOR THIRTY SECONDS
goal: A hidden preference often speaks when one door briefly closes.
steps: 1. Close Door — Picture the two leading options. Cross out one for thirty seconds and pretend it is unavailable; do not commit. Close Door — hear sound.
2. Read Protest — Notice the first specific reaction—relief, disappointment, bargaining, urgency, or no change. Name it in four words or fewer.
3. Reopen Choice — Uncross the option. Repeat once with the other door closed so both reactions receive the same test. Close Door — pick action.
4. Choose Next — Use the clearer reaction as one piece of data, then choose only the next responsible move. Close Door — next action.

title: VALUE BEFORE CERTAINTY
goal: When the Imagine a path is missing, choose the way of walking.
steps: 1. Ask Quality — Ask: ‘What quality do I want this next action to carry?’ Pick one—honesty, courage, care, fairness, patience. Value Before — feel support.
2. Look Single — Define how that quality would look in a single visible movement today. Value Before — split duty.
3. Let Certainty — Let certainty remain absent while the compass gives direction. Value Before — next action.

title: THE THIRD VOICE
goal: Emotion and logic are witnesses; wisdom gives the final answer.
steps: 1. Open Voices — Complete three lines. Third Voice — soften shoulders.
2. Name Feeling — FEELING SAYS: include its full truth.
3. Name Facts — FACTS SAY: include only verified information. Third Voice — name feeling.
4. Build Wisdom — WISE RESPONSE: honour the need in the first line and the constraints in the second.
5. Use Wisdom — Read only the third line before acting. Third Voice — next action.

4. Return Acceptance — If no, return to acceptance or support.
5. Stop Soothing — Do not keep using soothing when the door requires a key. Feeling Fixing — next action.

title: FINISH THE LOOK
goal: Defence narrows the world; sense of where you are reopens it.
steps: 1. Let Eyes — Let your eyes move before your head. Finish Look — soften shoulders.

4. Allow Neck — Allow the neck to follow only within comfort.
5. Place Attention — End by selecting where attention belongs now. Finish Look — next action.

title: ONE DROP, NOT THE OCEAN
goal: Small contact can process what flooding cannot.
steps: 1. Choose Tiniest — Choose the tiniest fragment of the difficult material: one edge, colour, word, or body sensation. Drop Ocean — feel support.
2. Return Fully — Contact it briefly, then return fully to a stabilising cue.
3. Find Dose — Hold the dose that allowed recovery. Drop Ocean — name sensation.
4. Use Less — Next practice uses the same or less—not an ambitious leap. Drop Ocean — next action.

title: TRACK WHAT HOLDS
goal: Support becomes stronger when it receives precise attention.
steps: 1. Locate Bodily — Locate one bodily sign of steadiness—warmth, pressure, uprightness, ease, or a capable impulse. Track Holds — press feet.
2. Describe Boundaries — Say its boundaries and changes for twenty seconds.
3. Ask Memory — Ask what memory, person, posture, or environment strengthens it by one degree. Track Holds — name feeling.
4. Add Ingredient — Add only that ingredient. Track Holds — next action.

title: LET BREATH BREATHE YOU
goal: Remove the manager from respiration.
steps: 1. Follow Breaths — Follow three natural breaths exactly as they occur. Let Breath — breathe naturally.
2. Leave Breath Alone — Do not deepen, slow, count, or improve them.
3. Start — Notice where each begins by itself and where it ends without instruction. Let Breath — notice detail.
4. Let Body — Between breaths, let the body choose again.
5. Witness Motion — Your only action is witnessing what already knows how to move. Let Breath — next action.

title: RHYTHM BEFORE DEPTH
goal: A sustainable cadence can organise the whole system.
steps: 1. Choose Slow — Choose a slow, comfortable pace in which inhale and exhale feel smooth. Rhythm Before — loosen hands.
2. Use Quiet — Use a quiet timer or gentle movement as metronome, never forcing lung volume. Rhythm Before — name sensation.
3. Continue Long — Continue long enough to find a repeatable rhythm, then remove the metronome and keep one easy cycle. Rhythm Before — next action.

title: THE EVEN BRIDGE
goal: Symmetry gives attention a simple crossing.
steps: 1. Pick Requires — Pick a count that requires no effort. Even Bridge — widen gaze.
2. Count Exhale — Inhale for that count, exhale for the same count, and leave any natural pause untouched.
3. Imagine Pair — Imagine each pair forming equal sides of a bridge. Even Bridge — name sensation.
4. Complete Few — Complete a few balanced crossings, then let counting dissolve. Even Bridge — next action.

title: WHAT SURVIVES THREE STATES?
goal: Compare experience across waking, dreaming, and dreamless sleep.
steps: 1. Picture Appears — Picture what appears in waking, what appears in dreams, and what is absent or inferred in deep sleep. Survives Three — hear sound.
2. Ask Claims — Ask which claims of identity remain supported across all three. Survives Three — challenge answer.
3. Hold Conclusions — Hold conclusions lightly; this is an inquiry into ongoing sense, not a demand for belief. Survives Three — next action.

goal: Extremes can impersonate discipline.
steps: 1. Rest Review — Review sleep, food, effort, practice, and rest. Sustainable Middle — loosen hands.

3. Set Middle — Set a middle range you could repeat for two weeks. Sustainable Middle — add counterfact.
4. Choose Smallest — Use the smallest adjustment that moves into that band today. Sustainable Middle — next action.

title: IMPACT IS KNOWN; MOTIVE IS PENDING
goal: Do not let mind-reading erase visible harm.
steps: 1. Separate Unknown — Picture three separate statements: their behaviour; what effect it had; what you do not know about intention. Impact Known — soften shoulders.
2. Base — Base your next boundary on behaviour and impact. Impact Known — allow opposite.
3. Leave Motive — Leave motive open until reliable evidence or direct communication updates it. Impact Known — next action.

title: MOTIVE: ACCESS DENIED
goal: Other minds are opaque until they speak and behave.
steps: 1. Catch Sentence — Catch the sentence ‘They think…’ or ‘They wanted…’. Motive Access — press feet.
2. Replace Possibilities — Replace it with three possibilities and one clear question.
3. Possibility — Notice each possibility as hypothesis, not evidence. Motive Access — challenge answer.
4. Choose Behaviour — Choose behaviour based on what is known while curiosity remains active. Motive Access — next action.

steps: 1. Choose Signals — Choose the two signals fighting for attention. Braid Signals — feel support.

4. Decide After — Decide only after the braid is complete. Braid Signals — next action.

title: MATCH THE PRESSURE, THEN ZERO IT
goal: Equal pressure gives restless energy a shared route down.
steps: 1. Press Equal — Press palms together—or both hands into one cushion—at about twenty percent effort. Keep breathing ordinary. Match Pressure — move slowly.
2. Match Force — Adjust until neither side wins and the pressure feels equal. Hold that match for two seconds.
3. Step Down — Lower both sides together through three gentle levels: fifteen, ten, then five percent. Match Pressure — name feeling.
4. Reach Zero — Reach zero, rest both hands on a stable surface, and observe whether the urge to press returns. Match Pressure — next action.

title: ASK THE QUESTION FEAR KEEPS ANSWERING
goal: Direct data can update the relationship model.
steps: 1. Picture Assumption — Picture the assumption driving your reaction. Ask Question — hear sound.
2. Question Whose — Convert it into one clear, non-leading question whose answer could prove the assumption wrong. Ask Question — challenge answer.
3. Ask Suitable — Ask at a suitable time, listen fully, and compare reply plus later behaviour with the original model. Ask Question — next action.

title: COUNT EVERY OPEN LOOP
goal: Invisible commitments keep using memory until named.
steps: 1. Question Task — Name every unresolved promise, question, task, decision, and waiting item without solving any. Count Every — loosen hands.
2. Use Line — Use one line each. Count Every — notice detail.
3. Imagine Boundary — When nothing else appears for thirty seconds, Imagine a boundary around the inventory and choose a separate processing time. Count Every — next action.

title: SEPARATE THE MENTAL INBOXES

steps: 1. Question Capture — Catch each mental item, then route it into IDEA, OBLIGATION, FEAR, MEMORY, or QUESTION. Separate Mental — breathe naturally.
2. Give Category — Give each category its own processing rule. Separate Mental — notice detail.
3. Don't Determine — Prioritise only after sorting, so emotional intensity does not determine inbox order. Separate Mental — next action.

3. Choose Action — Choose one action that acknowledges desire while keeping the valued asset intact. Want Now — next action.

title: THE BORING DOSE
goal: Low stimulation can be trained in measured exposure.
steps: 1. Choose Safe — Set up a boring task that is safe and preselect a short interval. Boring Dose — loosen hands.
2. Remove Entertainment — Remove entertainment but keep necessary tools.
3. Stay Boredom — Stay with boredom’s body sensations until the timer ends, then stop even if you could continue. Boring Dose — name sensation.
4. Increase — Increase future doses slowly. Boring Dose — next action.

title: WHAT PREPARATION DID WORRY ACTUALLY PRODUCE?
goal: Imagined work should show a deliverable.
steps: 1. Create Worry — Name every concrete preparation created by the worry. Preparation Did — soften shoulders.
2. Separate Useful — Separate useful actions from repeated simulation.
3. Prepare Name — If the Name contains a real gap, prepare once. Preparation Did — pick action.
4. Remain Name — If no gap remains, Name further worry UNPAID OVERTIME. Preparation Did — next action.

title: REPLAY THE TURNING POINT AT HALF SPEED
goal: Find the turning point, not another theory about the whole conversation.
steps: 1. Recall Exchange — Choose no more than ten seconds of the interaction, beginning before the moment that felt different. Replay Turning — breathe naturally.
2. Halve Speed — Replay it once in imagination at half speed. Keep to observable words, pauses, volume, face, and movement.
3. Shift — Stop at the first change and name it without motive: ‘the pause lengthened,’ ‘the volume rose,’ or ‘the reply shortened.’. Replay Turning — pick action.
4. Keep Fact — Keep that one fact. End the replay before building another explanation. Replay Turning — next action.

title: GIVE THOUGHTS WEIGHTED VOTES
goal: Mental statements should not all receive one ballot.
steps: 1. Score Evidence — For each influential thought, score evidence, relevant expertise, recency, and decision relevance. Give Thoughts — move slowly.
2. Multiply — Multiply nothing; simply rank. Give Thoughts — pick action.
3. Let Highest — Let the highest-quality thought advise the action while lower-ranked voices remain recorded but nonbinding. Give Thoughts — next action.

title: AUCTION THE NEXT ATTENTION BLOCK
goal: Limited thought needs a clear way to choose.
steps: 1. Let Active — Let each active concern bid on urgency, consequence, reversibility, and information value. Auction Next — loosen hands.
2. Total — Total the four ratings.
3. Protect Block — Award one protected block to the highest bidder and deny all others entry until time expires. Auction Next — pick action.
4. Update Evidence — Re-auction with updated evidence. Auction Next — next action.

title: TURN THE LOOP INTO FIVE ICONS
goal: A loop is easier to spot when it has to fit on five tiles.
steps: 1. No Sentences — Imagine five boxes. Do not use full sentences. Turn Loop — widen gaze.
2. Imagine Five Signs — Give each of the last five thought turns one simple mental picture.
3. Spot The Return — Notice the first picture whose meaning comes back later. Turn Loop — notice detail.
4. Choose An Exit — At the next box, picture one real fact to check or one small action to take, then stop imagining. Turn Loop — next action.

title: SCULPT THE PROBLEM
goal: Abstract distress changes when relationships become physical.
steps: 1. Use Small — Represent the problem using small objects for people, obstacles, resources, and goals. Sculpt Problem — feel support.
2. Feel Arrange — Arrange them as they feel now.
3. Move Object — Move only one object or distance to create a more workable configuration. Sculpt Problem — pick action.
4. Name Real — Name the real-life action equivalent to that move. Sculpt Problem — next action.

title: REMEMBER THE FUTURE IN ADVANCE
goal: Desired behaviour is easier when it feels feltly familiar.
steps: 1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action. Remember Future — breathe naturally.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared. Remember Future — name sensation.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and perform it now. Remember Future — next action.

1. Create Memory — Create a memory-like scene set just after completing the action. Remember Future — breathe naturally.
2. Include Time — Include time, location, body posture, one sensory cue, along with what you did when difficulty appeared. Remember Future — name sensation.
3. Look Backward — Look backward from that imagined completion to the first real movement and perform it now. Remember Future — next action.

WIN
✓ Desired behaviour is easier when it feels feltly familiar.

Create Memory → Include Time → Look Backward

PAUSE
Keep future scenes realistic rather than using fantasy as avoidance.

4. Test It — Try that small alter once. Imagine Inner — next action.

title: RUN A TWO-OPTION KNOCKOUT
goal: Crowded choices get clearer when only two enter each round.
steps: 1. Seed Options — Picture the available options into a simple bracket. Give an unpaired option a bye rather than inventing a rival. Two Option — soften shoulders.
2. Pick Criterion — Choose one criterion that matters for this round and Picture it above the bracket. Do not switch it mid-game.
3. Play Pairs — Compare only two options at a time. Advance the one that better meets the declared criterion. Two Option — notice detail.
4. Crown Next — Crown the final survivor as the next option to inspect or act on—not as a permanent life verdict. Two Option — next action.

title: THE PAST INVESTMENT GETS NO NEW VOTE
goal: Sunk cost is history, not future value.

2. Compare Options — Compare options from today forward using remaining cost, likely benefit, opportunity cost, and risk. Past Investment — pick action.
3. Reveal — Reveal the past investment afterward only for learning, never for sharing. Past Investment — next action.
